svg.aria-label: How to write ે: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing ે
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ે (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/6_ke.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the e sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>. Source note on variation: In the template for કે, and in all 33 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ે is one pen-down run that starts at the upper-left tip, arcs right and comes down to the lower right, where it meets the consonant. t30apps, already cited for એ, sweeps the matching high arc from left to right, last. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 162 of its 165 stored prototypes of the e sign (98%) are one stroke, most running from the upper left down to the lower right. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer.
